reviewer: Claude (independent read-only forensics; not the runtime qualification, which stays with Grok)
inputs: runs/m1-desktop-010/shared-shell-return-attempt001-console-early.bin (private, 1361 lines) and runs/m1-desktop-010/shared-shell-return001-early-forensics/ (session-result.txt, manager-status.log, per-instance application stdout/stderr logs). These are private target data, read as data.
question: What sent the first SIGKILL to APP14 (instance 0001..., pid 14)?
answer: NOT ESTABLISHED. The evidence excludes the manager, APP14's own PTY/child-group code, logged code-signing failures and the recurring vnode-alias kernel message. What remains consistent is a kernel-originated kill that logs nothing to the console, during or immediately after APP14's exec: a spawn-time process_signature failure, a jetsam kill or a guard exception. The data cannot tell these apart, because the kernel exit reason was not captured before the reap. I assign no cause.

observed.timeline_manager_ms: APP14: requested 246, Admission and StatusNonblocking 247, SpawnReturned and PidOwned 251, then status EOF, 'missing CLEANUP at EOF' and AppReaped all at 260 (raw wait 9 = WIFSIGNALED SIGKILL, no core). status_bytes 0. TermAttempt and KillAttempt are unset for attempt 0. APP15: SpawnReturned and PidOwned 258, TermAttempt 561, never reaped by the manager.
observed.c_spawn: Both attempts: native_return 0, stage 10, child_created 1, requested and observed flags 16398 (0x400e), all error fields 0, duplicate_count 4. posix_spawn reported success for both.
observed.app14_artifacts: The closed export shows DL11_RECORD_MISSING (errno 2) for all six app records, including pty-rx.bin, and APP14's application-stdout.log and application-stderr.log are 0 bytes. application.json is not part of either export, so whether it exists is unknown.
observed.app15_artifacts: APP15's stderr contains exactly 'chonk-terminal-darwin: status channel: Broken pipe (os error 32)'. Its six records were exported (rc 0), so the same binary ran its full startup, PTY and cleanup path.
observed.session: session-result: elapsed_ms 315, cleanup Incomplete, deadline false, frame_error None, manager_failed true. The console shows the PDGOP close, then 'IOGOP: console-return acquire-request result=0x00000000', then the frontend error 'managed signal scope failed ... cleanup: Incomplete ... seal_error ...' with restore=[].
observed.kernel_console_near_launch: Between the frontend's first [FB??-A-UC]::clientMemoryForType (00126004) and its clientClose (00126540), the only kernel lines are a pair of 'vnode_create_internal: alias vnode (vid = ...) is in state of change (start)/(end)' lines. There is no CODE SIGNING, load_code_signature, memorystatus, guard, sandbox or exec-failure line for pid 14 anywhere in the capture. AMFI is the PureDarwin permissive stub ('amfi: permissive stub registered'). Its earlier invalid-page events for launchd and launchctl were logged as 'allowing (remove VALID)'.

excluded_with_reason.manager_signal: OwnedApplications::service records TermAttempt or KillAttempt before any signal ('record intent first'), and neither gate is set for attempt 0. Its KILL also needs TERM plus 5 s, which is impossible inside 9-14 ms.
excluded_with_reason.app002_internal: In app002's run(), pty-rx.bin is created before Pty::shell forks the PTY child (main.rs, rx = log(..., "pty-rx.bin") then pty::Pty::shell). pty-rx.bin does not exist, so APP14 died before any PTY child existed. The app's only kill() sites are in Pty::cleanup, targeting that child or its group, and none could run. An ordinary setup error returns Err, which prints to stderr and exits 1 (wait 256), not SIGKILL with empty stderr.
excluded_with_reason.child_group: APP14 is its own process-group leader (POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP 0), and no PTY child existed. APP15's TERM (561) and its PTY cleanup came after APP14's death (260). The frontend's other kill() sites are generic chonk-shell paths, gated off in standalone per my 001-004 source reviews.
excluded_with_reason.logged_code_signing_failures: In pinned XNU, load_code_signature failures go through set_signature_error with printf('load_code_signature: ...') (mach_loader.c ~3770-3810). A LOAD_FAILURE would also make posix_spawn return an error, and it returned 0. cs_invalid_page logs 'allowing (remove VALID)' whenever it clears CS_VALID (kern_cs.c ~285-305). Its silent kill path needs CS_KILL. The app002 build (8003ec64, terminal-application-build-002) and the frontend are both ad-hoc linker-signed: CodeDirectory flags 0x20002 (CS_ADHOC|CS_LINKER_SIGNED), no CS_KILL, CS_HARD or runtime, and no entitlements or CMS. No such log line exists for pid 14.
excluded_with_reason.vnode_alias_message: That printf is specific to block-device (VBDEVVP) alias vnode creation (vfs_subr.c ~7255-7280). The same two-line pair appears in 11 earlier successful desktop/PDGOP-era captures (attempt-007 to 011, native-startup-001, native-live-001, passive-child-001, native-two-window-001, trackpad-enum-002, dart-survey-001), so it is not distinguishing evidence here.

consistent_but_unproven.spawn_time_process_signature_failure: In pinned XNU kern_exec.c (~8600-8830), for a spawn, failures from a MAC-policy exec return (ip_mac_return), launch constraints, signature/thread-state setup or the task access port cause psignal_vfork_with_reason(..., SIGKILL, reason) with error=0. posix_spawn therefore returns a PID and success while the child dies before running. This logs nothing to the console (KERNEL_DEBUG trace only) and matches the shape exactly. Three MAC policies are loaded (PureDarwin AMFI stub, PureDarwin Sandbox, vnguard). Nothing in the evidence shows why only the first of two back-to-back spawns of the same binary would fail.
consistent_but_unproven.other_silent_kernel_kills: Jetsam (memorystatus exit with SIGKILL) and fatal guard exceptions (OS_REASON_GUARD) also produce wait status 9 without any console printf in this capture, and are not excluded.
consistent_but_unproven.concurrency: The only observable difference between APP14 and APP15 is order and timing. The frontend spawned both in one service pass, about 5-7 ms apart, so APP15's posix_spawn of the same executable ran while APP14's first instructions would have been running. This is noted as a lead to test, not a cause.

diagnostic_recommendations_not_criteria_: Before reaping a child that exited, the manager could detect the exit with waitid(P_PID, pid, WEXITED|WNOHANG|WNOWAIT) and record proc_pidinfo(pid, PROC_PIDEXITREASONBASICINFO) for the zombie. Pinned XNU proc_info.c sets findzomb=1 for the EXITREASON flavors. That gives the kernel's own os_reason namespace and code (EXEC=9, CODESIGNING=3, JETSAM=1, GUARD=23, SECURITY=26 per sys/reason.h) and turns this from inference into a record.
A separate, explicitly labelled diagnostic boot with cs_debug=1 would make code-signing page events verbose.

A separately reviewed run that waits for the first app's READY (or adds a stagger) before the second startup request would test the concurrency lead. It must not be presented as a fix, and failed001 stays failed.
cross_check_note: The secondary failure (Astra's review) fits the 002 source: poll_desktop_shutdown returns Incomplete as soon as any application's completion is Incomplete. So after APP14's incomplete outcome, the coordinator sealed and exited at elapsed 315 without waiting for APP15's TERM, reap and CLEANUP. APP15 then hit the Broken pipe. My 002 review described that function but did not flag that the early return abandons the remaining apps' cleanup wait. I am recording that miss here.
